title: Transaction Boundaries: Uncommitted Work and Callouts in Apex

steps.prompt: An Apex service must update an Account status and immediately call an external credit verification REST API. If the callout occurs after the DML update in the same synchronous execution, what exception occurs and how should it be architected?

options.label: Throws System.CalloutException (uncommitted work); decouple using Queueable Apex or a published Platform Event
options.rationale: Salesforce transactions prohibit synchronous HTTP callouts when open DML mutations exist in the database thread. Decoupling via Queueable or Platform Event resets the transaction boundary.

options.label: Throws System.LimitException (callout after DML); wrap the callout in a Database.rollback(sp) savepoint block
options.distractorAntipattern: Setting or rolling back a Database Savepoint does not clear uncommitted database mutations to permit subsequent synchronous callouts in the same thread.
options.rationale: Setting or rolling back a Database Savepoint does not reset the transaction boundary to permit subsequent synchronous callouts in the same thread.

options.label: Throws System.AsyncException; annotate the callout method with @future(callout=true) and invoke it inline
options.distractorAntipattern: Calling an asynchronous method inline does not alter the synchronous thread execution or resolve open DML locks before the callout.
options.rationale: Future methods cannot accept sObject arguments, cannot be monitored via parent-child job IDs, and still throw CalloutException if executed within existing async contexts.
